bull.probability_evidence: Wizards of the Coast's margin expansion looks structural, not cyclical: ROIC rose from 10.4% (FY21) to 28.3% TTM, gross margin from 50.5% to 63.8%, and net debt/EBITDA fell from 5.72x to 1.92x (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/has/financials/ratios/); tabletop/WizCo revenue grew 30%/27% YoY per the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/46080/000004608026000050/has-20260628.htm).

target_band.cite: The evaluation's bull target (124.54) is the fact sheet's base-case fair value; its two anchors disagree (DCF 130.08 vs EV/EBITDA 113.45, factsheet-2026-10-09.md Fair value table), half-spread 8.315 / 124.54 = 6.68%.

base.probability_evidence: EV/EBITDA (12.0x) sits just above its own 5-year minimum (11.7x) and P/FCF (10.8x) is near its 5-year minimum (10.4x) (factsheet-2026-10-09.md Valuation table) — the market is pricing 'prove it for more quarters,' consistent with a flat-price base case rather than a re-rating or de-rating.

target_band.cite: Base case cites the same fact-sheet base fair-value anchors (DCF 130.08 vs EV/EBITDA 113.45, factsheet-2026-10-09.md Fair value table), half-spread 8.315, relative to the 92.50 target = 8.99%.

bear.probability_evidence: EV/Sales (3.1x) is already above its own 5-year maximum (3.0x, factsheet-2026-10-09.md Valuation table), and 58% of revenue depends on one hit-driven card franchise (Wizards of the Coast tabletop +30% YoY on Magic releases, 10-Q MD&A) — a real risk that the mix-shift/margin cycle normalises.

target_band.cite: Bear fair-value anchors disagree sharply (DCF-bear 7.84 vs EV/EBITDA-bear 89.29, factsheet-2026-10-09.md Fair value table), half-spread 40.73 / 69.50 = 58.6% — far above the measured residual volatility, so capped at the mc-inputs.json blended residual volatility (26.00%), the script's hard ceiling (montecarlo.py: target_band must not exceed residual_vol.blended).
